newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Mozambique accepts businessman's tourism proposal.
newsitem.headline: Mozambique accepts businessman's tourism proposal.

text.p: The Mozambican government has approved a multi-million dollar tourism project presented by a millionaire American who backed a former rebel movement, the Maputo daily Mediafax said on Wednesday.
American magnate James Blanchard presented his 800 million dollar plan for a 216,000 hectare wildlife paradise to the government last year.
He said it would include a railway line, luxury housing, floating casinos and added that local farmers would be able to access satelitte television.
The government has not formally announced its acceptance of the project, but senior civil service sources told Reuters they believe the Medifax story was true.
The decision was apparently taken at a cabinet meeting last month.
Blanchard supported Mozambique National Resistance (Renamo) rebels in their 16-year war against the government. The rebels were backed by the apartheid regime in South Africa.
Renamo was defeated by President Joachim Chissano's ruling Frelimo Party in multi-party elections in 1994. Renamo is now the biggest opposition party in parliament.
But Chissano and Blanchard now seem to have put the past behind them and were photographed together when Blanchard visited Mozambique earlier this year.
Satellite television for peasant farmers in the area is also thrown in, according to the project report presented by Blanc hard last year.
